﴿Or do they say: he has fabricated it?﴾ That is: he invented the Qur'an from his own self and forged it. "Al-taqawwul" is generally used only for lying, although its root meaning is the affectation of speech. From it comes "iqtāla ʿalayhi," and "iqtāla ʿalayhi" means "to rule over him." From it is the poet's saying:

And a station in a house of truth and felicity, and no physician has ruled over me in judgment.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, turned away from His saying "taqawwulahu" and moved to what is more shameful for them, saying: ﴿Rather, they do not believe﴾. That is: the reason these contradictory statements issue from them is that they are disbelievers who do not believe in Allah and do not affirm what His Messenger ﷺ brought.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, challenged them and established the proof against them, saying: ﴿Then let them produce a discourse like it﴾. That is: like the Qur'an in its composition, its excellence of expression, and its wondrous style, ﴿if they are truthful﴾ in what they claim: that Muhammad ﷺ fabricated it and brought it from his own self, although it is an Arabic discourse, and they are the chiefs and eloquent men of the Arabs, and the practitioners of all Arabic forms, in verse and prose.

Saʿid ibn Mansur, Hannad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi have transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: Indeed Allah raises the offspring of a believer to be with him in his rank in Paradise, even if they are below him in deeds, so that his eye may be comforted by them. Then he recited: ﴿And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith﴾, the verse.

Al-Bazzar and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted it from him as a raised (marfūʿ) report.

Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh also transmitted from him that the Prophet ﷺ said: "When a man enters Paradise, he asks about his parents, his wife and his children, and it is said: 'They have not reached your rank and your deeds.' He says: 'O Lord, I did my deeds for myself and for them.' So he is commanded to join them to him." And Ibn ʿAbbas recited: ﴿And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith﴾, the verse.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 52, verses 21–34 (part 2 of 2):

Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated in the Zawa'id of the Musnad, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the believers and their offspring are in Paradise, and indeed the polytheists and their offspring are in the Fire." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And those who believed...﴾ the verse. Its chain is as follows.

Abdullah ibn Ahmad said: Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Uthman, from Zadhan, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: "Khadijah asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about two sons who had died to her in the Jahiliyyah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'They are in the Fire.' When he saw the aversion in her face, he said: 'If you saw their place, you would hate them.' She said: 'O Messenger of Allah, then what of my child by you?' He said: 'In Paradise.' Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed the believers and their offspring are in Paradise, and indeed the polytheists and their offspring are in the Fire.' Then he recited: ﴿And those who believed...﴾ the verse."

Imam Ahmad said in the Musnad: Yazid narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah raises the rank of the righteous servant in Paradise, so he says: 'O Lord, from where is this for me?' And He says: 'By the forgiveness of your child for you.'" Its chain is sound (sahih).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Hakim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿And We did not deprive them﴾ that he said: "We did not diminish them."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding ﴿No idle talk therein﴾ that he said: "(p-1415) Falsehood, ﴿nor sinful speech﴾ he said: lying."

al-Bazzar narrated from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, they will long for their brothers. The couch of one will come until it is level with the couch of the other, and they will converse, and one will recline and the other will recline, and they will talk about what they did in the world. One of them will say: 'O so-and-so, do you know which day Allah forgave us? The day we were in such-and-such a place, and we called upon Allah, and He forgave us.'"

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Aishah, who said: "If Allah were to open for the people of the earth from the torment of the scorching wind (al-samum) the amount of a fingertip, it would burn the earth and whoever is upon it."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿Indeed He is the Most Kind (al-Barr)﴾ that he said: "al-Latif (the Subtle, the Gentle)."

Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Jarir narrated from him that when the Quraysh gathered at Dar al-Nadwah (the assembly house) concerning the matter of the Prophet (ﷺ), one of them said: "Bind him in chains, and wait for him the vicissitudes of time (al-manun) until he dies as those before him died among the poets: Zuhayr and al-Nabighah. He is only like one of them." So Allah revealed concerning that: ﴿Or do they say, "A poet; we await for him the misfortune of time"?﴾

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding His saying ﴿the misfortune of time (raybal-manun)﴾ that he said: "Death."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 52, verses 35–49:

His saying: ﴿Or were they created of nothing?﴾ Here "am" (أم) is the disjunctive (munqati'a) one, as has been explained in what precedes it and as will come in what follows it: meaning, "Rather, were they created in this wondrous manner and marvelous craftsmanship without a creator for them?"

Al-Zajjaj said: That is, were they created in vain, for nothing, not to be called to account, not to be commanded, and not to be forbidden? He took "min" (مِن) to mean "li" (اللام, "for").

Ibn Kaysan said: Were they created in vain and left neglected (sudan), not commanded and not forbidden?

It was also said: The meaning is: Were they created without father or mother, so that they are like inanimate matter, not understanding and not bearing any proof against them? ﴿Or are they the creators?﴾ That is, "Rather, do they say they created themselves, so they are not commanded or forbidden, even though they admit that Allah is their creator? And if they admit it, the proof is binding upon them."

﴿Or did they create the heavens and the earth?﴾ They do not claim this, so the proof is binding upon them. For this reason He turned away from this and said: ﴿Nay, they have no certainty﴾, that is, they are not certain of the matter, but rather they grope in the darkness of doubt regarding Allah's promise and His threat.

﴿Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord?﴾ That is, the treasuries of the provision of the servants. It was also said: the keys of mercy.

Muqatil said: He says: Do they hold the keys of your Lord through prophethood, so that they place them wherever they wish? Likewise said Ikrimah. Al-Kalbi said: the treasuries of rain and provision. ﴿Or are they the overseers?﴾ That is, the dominant, the tyrannical.

In al-Sihah it says: al-musaytir (المُسَيْطِرُ) is one who is set over a thing to oversee it, to look after its affairs and record its deeds; its root is from al-satr (السَّطْر, "line"), because the book is written in lines (yusattar).

Abu 'Ubayda said: "Sattarta 'alayya" means: you made me a servant to you.

The majority read al-musaytirun with a pure ṣād (الصاد الخالصة). Ibn Muhaysin, Humayd, Mujahid, Qunbul and Hisham read it with a pure sīn (السين الخالصة). This reading is also narrated from Hafs. Khallad read it with a ṣād mushammah zāy.

﴿Or do they have a ladder by which they listen?﴾ That is, "Rather, do they claim that they have a ladder set up to the heaven, by which they ascend and listen therein to the speech of the angels and what is revealed to them, and reach knowledge of the unseen just as Muhammad (ﷺ) reaches it by way of revelation?"

His saying "fīhi" (فِيهِ) is an attribute of "sullam" (سُلَّم). It is in its original locative sense, and it was also said it means "ʿalā" (عَلى): that is, they listen upon it, like His saying: ﴿And I will crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees﴾. This was said by al-Akhfash.

Abu 'Ubayda said: they listen by means of it.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that they are like Gabriel, who comes to the Prophet (ﷺ) with revelation. It was also said that it is in a accusative position as a circumstantial (ḥāl): that is, ascending upon it. ﴿So let their listener bring a clear authority﴾ if they claim that, that is, with a manifest, evident proof.

﴿Or does He have daughters while you have sons?﴾ That is, "Rather, do you attribute daughters to Allah while you have sons?" He, glorified be He, mocked their intellects, misled their minds and rebuked them: that is, they ascribe to Allah daughters, which are the weaker of the two kinds, and they assign to themselves sons, which are the higher of the two. This implies that whoever holds this view is in a lowly place in understanding and intellect, so it is not far-fetched from him to deny resurrection and reject monotheism.

Then He, glorified be He, returned to addressing His Messenger (ﷺ) and said: ﴿Or do you ask them for a payment?﴾ That is, "Rather, do you ask them for a payment they would give you for conveying the message?" ﴿So they are burdened with debt﴾, that is, burdened with an undertaking of a fine you demand from them: that is, they are overwhelmed by bearing that heavy debt.

Qatadah said: He says: Did you ask these people for a reward, so that it burdens them and they cannot accept Islam?

﴿Or do they have the unseen, so they write it down?﴾ That is, "Rather, do they claim that they have knowledge of the unseen, which is what is in the Preserved Tablet, so that they write for people whatever they wish of the knowledge of the unseen?"

Qatadah said: This is an answer to their saying: ﴿We await for him the misfortunes of time﴾. Allah says: Or do they have the unseen, so that they know Muhammad will die before them, so that they write it?

Ibn Qutaybah said: the meaning of "yaktubun" (يَكْتُبُونَ) is that they judge by what they say.

﴿Or do they intend a plot?﴾ That is, a scheme against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so that they destroy him by that scheme. ﴿Then those who disbelieve, they are the ones plotted against﴾, that is, the ones upon whom their scheme is turned and who will be repaid for their plotting; the harm of their plot returns to them. ﴿And the evil plot does not encompass except its people﴾ [Fatir: 43]. Allah killed them on the day of Badr and humiliated them on more than one occasion, and He, glorified be He, plotted against them: ﴿And they plotted, and Allah plotted, and Allah is the best of planners﴾ [Al 'Imran: 54].

﴿Or do they have a god other than Allah?﴾ That is, "Rather, do they claim that they have a god other than Allah who protects them, provides for them and helps them?"

Then He, glorified be He, declared Himself free of this hideous assertion and said: ﴿Glory be to Allah above what they associate﴾, that is, above their associating (others) with Him, or above those they make partners to Him.

Then He, glorified be He, mentioned some of their ignorance and said: ﴿And if they should see a piece of the sky falling, they would say, "Layered clouds."﴾ Kisf is the plural of kisfah, which is a piece of a thing. The accusative of "sāqiṭan" (ساقِطًا) is circumstantial, or it is the second object. "Markum" means that which is piled up, one part upon another.

The meaning: If they were to see a piece of the sky falling upon them as punishment for them, they would not desist from their disbelief, but would say it is clouds piled up, one upon another. The differences of the readers regarding "kisfan" has already been mentioned.

Al-Akhfash said: Whoever reads "kisfan" (with a kasra on the kaf and a sukun on the sin) makes it singular, and whoever reads "kisafan" (with a kasra on the kaf and a fatḥa on the sin) makes it plural.

Then Allah, glorified be He, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to leave them, and said: ﴿So leave them until they meet their day in which they will be struck senseless﴾, that is, leave them and let them be until they meet the day of their death, or the day of their killing at Badr, or the Day of Resurrection.

The majority read "yulāqū" (يُلاقُوا); Abu Haywah read "yalqaw" (يَلْقَوْا). The majority read "yuṣ'aqūna" with the active form; Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim read it in the passive form. The ṣaʿqah (الصعقة) is destruction, as its explanation has already preceded.

﴿The day their plot will not avail them anything﴾: this is a substitute for "their day": that is, on that day their plot which they plotted against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in this world will not benefit them. ﴿Nor will they be helped﴾, that is, no helper will prevent the punishment descending upon them; rather, it will befall them without doubt.

﴿And indeed for those who have wronged there is a punishment besides that﴾, that is, for those who wronged themselves through disbelief and sins there is a punishment in this world, short of the punishment of the Day of Resurrection: that is, before it, and it is their being killed on the day of Badr.

Ibn Zayd said: It is the calamities of the world: pains, illnesses and afflictions, and the loss of wealth and children.

Mujahid said: It is hunger and hardship for seven years. It was said: it is the punishment of the grave. It was said: the intended punishment is drought, and the punishment that comes after it is their killing on the day of Badr. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾ what they will come to of Allah's punishment, and what He has prepared for them in this world and the Hereafter.

﴿And be patient for the judgment of your Lord﴾, until the punishment that We promised them befalls them. ﴿For indeed, you are in Our eyes﴾, that is, in Our sight and view, and in Our protection and safeguarding, so do not concern yourself with them.

Al-Zajjaj said: You are where We see you, guard you and watch over you, so they cannot reach you. ﴿And exalt your Lord with praise when you arise﴾, that is, declare your Lord free of what is unfitting for Him, joining that with praise of your Lord for His favor upon you, when you rise from your sitting place.

'Ata', Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Sufyan al-Thawri and Abu al-Ahwas said: He glorifies Allah when he rises from his sitting, saying: "Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi" or "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika" upon rising from every gathering he sits in.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b, al-Dahhak and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: When you rise to prayer.

Al-Dahhak said: He says: "Allahu akbar kabiran, wal-hamdu lillahi kathiran, wa subhan Allahi bukratan wa asilan." There is a difficulty in this, because the takbir occurs after rising, not during rising, and the tasbih occurs after the takbir, and this is not the meaning of the verse; so the first (view) is more preferable.

It was also said the meaning is: Pray to Allah when you rise from your sleep. Abu al-Jawza' and Hassan ibn 'Atiyyah said this.

Al-Kalbi said: Remember Allah with the tongue when you rise from your bed until you enter the prayer, which is the Fajr prayer.

﴿And during the night, glorify Him﴾: Allah, glorified be He, commanded him to glorify Him during part of the night. Muqatil said: that is, pray Maghrib and 'Isha'. It was also said: the two rak'ahs of Fajr. ﴿And after the setting of the stars﴾, that is, at the time of their receding at the end of the night. It was said: the Fajr prayer, and Ibn Jarir preferred this. It was also said: it is glorification during the receding of the prayers. The majority read "idbār" (إدبارَ) with a kasra on the hamza, as a verbal noun. Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, Muhammad ibn al-Sumayfa', Ya'qub and al-Minhal ibn 'Amr read it with a fatḥa on the hamza, as a plural: that is, the ends and backs of the stars when they set. "Dubur al-amr" means its last part. The discussion of this has already preceded in Surat Qaf.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Or are they the overseers?﴾ that he said: the dominant ones.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him: ﴿Or are they the ones who bring down?﴾

They also narrated from him regarding ﴿a punishment besides that﴾: that he said it is the punishment of the grave before the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Barzah al-Aslami who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in his later life, when he rose from a gathering, would say: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, ashhadu an la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayk.' A man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you say a statement you did not used to say before?' He said: 'It is an expiation for what occurs in the gathering.'"

Al-Nasa'i and al-Hakim also narrated it from the hadith of al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Rafi' ibn Khadij, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir narrated from Abu Hurayrah from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever sits in a gathering in which there is much noise, and says before he rises from his gathering: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, ashhadu an la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayk,' he will be forgiven for whatever occurred in that gathering."

al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan sahih.

There are supported and mursal narrations on this topic.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And exalt your Lord with praise when you arise﴾ that he said: when you rise from your bed until you enter into prayer.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Hurayrah from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding His saying: ﴿And during the night, glorify Him﴾ that he said: "The two rak'ahs before the Fajr prayer."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿and after the setting of the stars﴾ that he said: the two rak'ahs of Fajr.

Ibn Kaysan said: Were they created in vain and left neglected (sudan), not commanded and not forbidden?

It was also said: The meaning is: Were they created without father or mother, so that they are like inanimate matter, not understanding and not bearing any proof against them? ﴿Or are they the creators?﴾ That is, "Rather, do they say they created themselves, so they are not commanded or forbidden, even though they admit that Allah is their creator? For this reason He turned away from this and said: ﴿Nay, they have no certainty﴾, that is, they are not certain of the matter, but rather they grope in the darkness of doubt regarding Allah's promise and His threat.

﴿Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord?﴾ That is, the treasuries of the provision of the servants. It was also said: the keys of mercy.

Muqatil said: He says: Do they hold the keys of your Lord through prophethood, so that they place them wherever they wish? Likewise said Ikrimah. Al-Kalbi said: the treasuries of rain and provision. ﴿Or are they the overseers?﴾ That is, the dominant, the tyrannical.

Abu 'Ubayda said: "Sattarta 'alayya" means: you made me a servant to you.

It was also said that it is in a accusative position as a circumstantial (ḥāl): that is, ascending upon it. ﴿So let their listener bring a clear authority﴾ if they claim that, that is, with a manifest, evident proof.

Qatadah said: He says: Did you ask these people for a reward, so that it burdens them and they cannot accept Islam?

Ibn Kaysan said: Were they created in vain and left neglected (sudan), not commanded and not forbidden?

It was also said: The meaning is: Were they created without father or mother, so that they are like inanimate matter, not understanding and not bearing any proof against them? ﴿Or are they the creators?﴾ That is, "Rather, do they say they created themselves, so they are not commanded or forbidden, even though they admit that Allah is their creator? And if they admit it, the proof is binding upon them."

﴿Or did they create the heavens and the earth?﴾ They do not claim this, so the proof is binding upon them. For this reason He turned away from this and said: ﴿Nay, they have no certainty﴾, that is, they are not certain of the matter, but rather they grope in the darkness of doubt regarding Allah's promise and His threat.

﴿Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord?﴾ That is, the treasuries of the provision of the servants. It was also said: the keys of mercy.

Muqatil said: He says: Do they hold the keys of your Lord through prophethood, so that they place them wherever they wish? Likewise said Ikrimah. Al-Kalbi said: the treasuries of rain and provision. ﴿Or are they the overseers?﴾ That is, the dominant, the tyrannical.

In al-Sihah it says: al-musaytir (المُسَيْطِرُ) is one who is set over a thing to oversee it, to look after its affairs and record its deeds; its root is from al-satr (السَّطْر, "line"), because the book is written in lines (yusattar).

Abu 'Ubayda said: "Sattarta 'alayya" means: you made me a servant to you.

﴿Or do they have a ladder by which they listen?﴾ That is, "Rather, do they claim that they have a ladder set up to the heaven, by which they ascend and listen therein to the speech of the angels and what is revealed to them, and reach knowledge of the unseen just as Muhammad (ﷺ) reaches it by way of revelation?"

His saying "fīhi" (فِيهِ) is an attribute of "sullam" (سُلَّم). It is in its original locative sense, and it was also said it means "ʿalā" (عَلى): that is, they listen upon it, like His saying: ﴿And I will crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees﴾. This was said by al-Akhfash.

Abu 'Ubayda said: they listen by means of it.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that they are like Gabriel, who comes to the Prophet (ﷺ) with revelation. It was also said that it is in a accusative position as a circumstantial (ḥāl): that is, ascending upon it. ﴿So let their listener bring a clear authority﴾ if they claim that, that is, with a manifest, evident proof.

Then He, glorified be He, returned to addressing His Messenger (ﷺ) and said: ﴿Or do you ask them for a payment?﴾ That is, "Rather, do you ask them for a payment they would give you for conveying the message?" ﴿So they are burdened with debt﴾, that is, burdened with an undertaking of a fine you demand from them: that is, they are overwhelmed by bearing that heavy debt.

Qatadah said: He says: Did you ask these people for a reward, so that it burdens them and they cannot accept Islam?

﴿Or do they have the unseen, so they write it down?﴾ That is, "Rather, do they claim that they have knowledge of the unseen, which is what is in the Preserved Tablet, so that they write for people whatever they wish of the knowledge of the unseen?"

Qatadah said: This is an answer to their saying: ﴿We await for him the misfortunes of time﴾. Allah says: Or do they have the unseen, so that they know Muhammad will die before them, so that they write it?

Ibn Qutaybah said: the meaning of "yaktubun" (يَكْتُبُونَ) is that they judge by what they say.

﴿Or do they intend a plot?﴾ That is, a scheme against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so that they destroy him by that scheme. ﴿Then those who disbelieve, they are the ones plotted against﴾, that is, the ones upon whom their scheme is turned and who will be repaid for their plotting; the harm of their plot returns to them. ﴿And the evil plot does not encompass except its people﴾ [Fatir: 43]. Ibn Kaysan said: Were they created in vain and left neglected (sudan), not commanded and not forbidden?

It was also said: The meaning is: Were they created without father or mother, so that they are like inanimate matter, not understanding and not bearing any proof against them? ﴿Or are they the creators?﴾ That is, "Rather, do they say they created themselves, so they are not commanded or forbidden, even though they admit that Allah is their creator? And if they admit it, the proof is binding upon them."

﴿Or did they create the heavens and the earth?﴾ They do not claim this, so the proof is binding upon them. For this reason He turned away from this and said: ﴿Nay, they have no certainty﴾, that is, they are not certain of the matter, but rather they grope in the darkness of doubt regarding Allah's promise and His threat.

﴿Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord?﴾ That is, the treasuries of the provision of the servants. It was also said: the keys of mercy.

Muqatil said: He says: Do they hold the keys of your Lord through prophethood, so that they place them wherever they wish? Likewise said Ikrimah. Al-Kalbi said: the treasuries of rain and provision. ﴿Or are they the overseers?﴾ That is, the dominant, the tyrannical.

In al-Sihah it says: al-musaytir (المُسَيْطِرُ) is one who is set over a thing to oversee it, to look after its affairs and record its deeds; its root is from al-satr (السَّطْر, "line"), because the book is written in lines (yusattar).

Abu 'Ubayda said: "Sattarta 'alayya" means: you made me a servant to you.

The majority read al-musaytirun with a pure ṣād (الصاد الخالصة). Ibn Muhaysin, Humayd, Mujahid, Qunbul and Hisham read it with a pure sīn (السين الخالصة). This reading is also narrated from Hafs. Khallad read it with a ṣād mushammah zāy.

﴿Or do they have a ladder by which they listen?﴾ That is, "Rather, do they claim that they have a ladder set up to the heaven, by which they ascend and listen therein to the speech of the angels and what is revealed to them, and reach knowledge of the unseen just as Muhammad (ﷺ) reaches it by way of revelation?"

His saying "fīhi" (فِيهِ) is an attribute of "sullam" (سُلَّم). It is in its original locative sense, and it was also said it means "ʿalā" (عَلى): that is, they listen upon it, like His saying: ﴿And I will crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees﴾. This was said by al-Akhfash.

Abu 'Ubayda said: they listen by means of it.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that they are like Gabriel, who comes to the Prophet (ﷺ) with revelation. It was also said that it is in a accusative position as a circumstantial (ḥāl): that is, ascending upon it. ﴿So let their listener bring a clear authority﴾ if they claim that, that is, with a manifest, evident proof.

﴿Or does He have daughters while you have sons?﴾ That is, "Rather, do you attribute daughters to Allah while you have sons?" He, glorified be He, mocked their intellects, misled their minds and rebuked them: that is, they ascribe to Allah daughters, which are the weaker of the two kinds, and they assign to themselves sons, which are the higher of the two. This implies that whoever holds this view is in a lowly place in understanding and intellect, so it is not far-fetched from him to deny resurrection and reject monotheism.

Then He, glorified be He, returned to addressing His Messenger (ﷺ) and said: ﴿Or do you ask them for a payment?﴾ That is, "Rather, do you ask them for a payment they would give you for conveying the message?" ﴿So they are burdened with debt﴾, that is, burdened with an undertaking of a fine you demand from them: that is, they are overwhelmed by bearing that heavy debt.

Qatadah said: He says: Did you ask these people for a reward, so that it burdens them and they cannot accept Islam?

﴿Or do they have the unseen, so they write it down?﴾ That is, "Rather, do they claim that they have knowledge of the unseen, which is what is in the Preserved Tablet, so that they write for people whatever they wish of the knowledge of the unseen?"

Qatadah said: This is an answer to their saying: ﴿We await for him the misfortunes of time﴾. Allah says: Or do they have the unseen, so that they know Muhammad will die before them, so that they write it?

Ibn Qutaybah said: the meaning of "yaktubun" (يَكْتُبُونَ) is that they judge by what they say.

﴿Or do they intend a plot?﴾ That is, a scheme against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so that they destroy him by that scheme. ﴿Then those who disbelieve, they are the ones plotted against﴾, that is, the ones upon whom their scheme is turned and who will be repaid for their plotting; the harm of their plot returns to them. ﴿And the evil plot does not encompass except its people﴾ [Fatir: 43]. Allah killed them on the day of Badr and humiliated them on more than one occasion, and He, glorified be He, plotted against them: ﴿And they plotted, and Allah plotted, and Allah is the best of planners﴾ [Al 'Imran: 54].

﴿Or do they have a god other than Allah?﴾ That is, "Rather, do they claim that they have a god other than Allah who protects them, provides for them and helps them?"

Then He, glorified be He, declared Himself free of this hideous assertion and said: ﴿Glory be to Allah above what they associate﴾, that is, above their associating (others) with Him, or above those they make partners to Him.

Then He, glorified be He, mentioned some of their ignorance and said: ﴿And if they should see a piece of the sky falling, they would say, "Layered clouds."﴾ Kisf is the plural of kisfah, which is a piece of a thing. The accusative of "sāqiṭan" (ساقِطًا) is circumstantial, or it is the second object. "Markum" means that which is piled up, one part upon another.

The meaning: If they were to see a piece of the sky falling upon them as punishment for them, they would not desist from their disbelief, but would say it is clouds piled up, one upon another. The differences of the readers regarding "kisfan" has already been mentioned.

Al-Akhfash said: Whoever reads "kisfan" (with a kasra on the kaf and a sukun on the sin) makes it singular, and whoever reads "kisafan" (with a kasra on the kaf and a fatḥa on the sin) makes it plural.

Then Allah, glorified be He, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to leave them, and said: ﴿So leave them until they meet their day in which they will be struck senseless﴾, that is, leave them and let them be until they meet the day of their death, or the day of their killing at Badr, or the Day of Resurrection.

The majority read "yulāqū" (يُلاقُوا); Abu Haywah read "yalqaw" (يَلْقَوْا). The majority read "yuṣ'aqūna" with the active form; Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim read it in the passive form. The ṣaʿqah (الصعقة) is destruction, as its explanation has already preceded.

Mujahid said: It is hunger and hardship for seven years. It was said: it is the punishment of the grave. Muhammad ibn Ka'b, al-Dahhak and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: When you rise to prayer.

Al-Dahhak said: He says: "Allahu akbar kabiran, wal-hamdu lillahi kathiran, wa subhan Allahi bukratan wa asilan." There is a difficulty in this, because the takbir occurs after rising, not during rising, and the tasbih occurs after the takbir, and this is not the meaning of the verse; so the first (view) is more preferable.

It was also said the meaning is: Pray to Allah when you rise from your sleep. Abu al-Jawza' and Hassan ibn 'Atiyyah said this.

Al-Kalbi said: Remember Allah with the tongue when you rise from your bed until you enter the prayer, which is the Fajr prayer.

﴿And during the night, glorify Him﴾: Allah, glorified be He, commanded him to glorify Him during part of the night. Muqatil said: that is, pray Maghrib and 'Isha'. It was also said: the two rak'ahs of Fajr. ﴿And after the setting of the stars﴾, that is, at the time of their receding at the end of the night. It was said: the Fajr prayer, and Ibn Jarir preferred this. It was also said: it is glorification during the receding of the prayers. The majority read "idbār" (إدبارَ) with a kasra on the hamza, as a verbal noun. Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, Muhammad ibn al-Sumayfa', Ya'qub and al-Minhal ibn 'Amr read it with a fatḥa on the hamza, as a plural: that is, the ends and backs of the stars when they set. "Dubur al-amr" means its last part. The discussion of this has already preceded in Surat Qaf.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 52, verses 35–49:

His saying: ﴿Or were they created of nothing?﴾ Here "am" (أم) is the disjunctive (munqati'a) one, as has been explained in what precedes it and as will come in what follows it: meaning, "Rather, were they created in this wondrous manner and marvelous craftsmanship without a creator for them?"

Al-Zajjaj said: That is, were they created in vain, for nothing, not to be called to account, not to be commanded, and not to be forbidden? He took "min" (مِن) to mean "li" (اللام, "for").

Ibn Kaysan said: Were they created in vain and left neglected (sudan), not commanded and not forbidden?

It was also said: The meaning is: Were they created without father or mother, so that they are like inanimate matter, not understanding and not bearing any proof against them? ﴿Or are they the creators?﴾ That is, "Rather, do they say they created themselves, so they are not commanded or forbidden, even though they admit that Allah is their creator? And if they admit it, the proof is binding upon them."

﴿Or did they create the heavens and the earth?﴾ They do not claim this, so the proof is binding upon them. For this reason He turned away from this and said: ﴿Nay, they have no certainty﴾, that is, they are not certain of the matter, but rather they grope in the darkness of doubt regarding Allah's promise and His threat.

﴿Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord?﴾ That is, the treasuries of the provision of the servants. It was also said: the keys of mercy.

Muqatil said: He says: Do they hold the keys of your Lord through prophethood, so that they place them wherever they wish? Likewise said Ikrimah. Al-Kalbi said: the treasuries of rain and provision. ﴿Or are they the overseers?﴾ That is, the dominant, the tyrannical.

In al-Sihah it says: al-musaytir (المُسَيْطِرُ) is one who is set over a thing to oversee it, to look after its affairs and record its deeds; its root is from al-satr (السَّطْر, "line"), because the book is written in lines (yusattar).

Abu 'Ubayda said: "Sattarta 'alayya" means: you made me a servant to you.

The majority read al-musaytirun with a pure ṣād (الصاد الخالصة). Ibn Muhaysin, Humayd, Mujahid, Qunbul and Hisham read it with a pure sīn (السين الخالصة). This reading is also narrated from Hafs. Khallad read it with a ṣād mushammah zāy.

﴿Or do they have a ladder by which they listen?﴾ That is, "Rather, do they claim that they have a ladder set up to the heaven, by which they ascend and listen therein to the speech of the angels and what is revealed to them, and reach knowledge of the unseen just as Muhammad (ﷺ) reaches it by way of revelation?"

His saying "fīhi" (فِيهِ) is an attribute of "sullam" (سُلَّم). It is in its original locative sense, and it was also said it means "ʿalā" (عَلى): that is, they listen upon it, like His saying: ﴿And I will crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees﴾. This was said by al-Akhfash.

Abu 'Ubayda said: they listen by means of it.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that they are like Gabriel, who comes to the Prophet (ﷺ) with revelation. It was also said that it is in a accusative position as a circumstantial (ḥāl): that is, ascending upon it. ﴿So let their listener bring a clear authority﴾ if they claim that, that is, with a manifest, evident proof.

﴿Or does He have daughters while you have sons?﴾ That is, "Rather, do you attribute daughters to Allah while you have sons?" He, glorified be He, mocked their intellects, misled their minds and rebuked them: that is, they ascribe to Allah daughters, which are the weaker of the two kinds, and they assign to themselves sons, which are the higher of the two. This implies that whoever holds this view is in a lowly place in understanding and intellect, so it is not far-fetched from him to deny resurrection and reject monotheism.

Then He, glorified be He, returned to addressing His Messenger (ﷺ) and said: ﴿Or do you ask them for a payment?﴾ That is, "Rather, do you ask them for a payment they would give you for conveying the message?" ﴿So they are burdened with debt﴾, that is, burdened with an undertaking of a fine you demand from them: that is, they are overwhelmed by bearing that heavy debt.

Qatadah said: He says: Did you ask these people for a reward, so that it burdens them and they cannot accept Islam?

﴿Or do they have the unseen, so they write it down?﴾ That is, "Rather, do they claim that they have knowledge of the unseen, which is what is in the Preserved Tablet, so that they write for people whatever they wish of the knowledge of the unseen?"

Qatadah said: This is an answer to their saying: ﴿We await for him the misfortunes of time﴾. Allah says: Or do they have the unseen, so that they know Muhammad will die before them, so that they write it?

Ibn Qutaybah said: the meaning of "yaktubun" (يَكْتُبُونَ) is that they judge by what they say.

﴿Or do they intend a plot?﴾ That is, a scheme against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so that they destroy him by that scheme. ﴿Then those who disbelieve, they are the ones plotted against﴾, that is, the ones upon whom their scheme is turned and who will be repaid for their plotting; the harm of their plot returns to them. ﴿And the evil plot does not encompass except its people﴾ [Fatir: 43]. Allah killed them on the day of Badr and humiliated them on more than one occasion, and He, glorified be He, plotted against them: ﴿And they plotted, and Allah plotted, and Allah is the best of planners﴾ [Al 'Imran: 54].

﴿Or do they have a god other than Allah?﴾ That is, "Rather, do they claim that they have a god other than Allah who protects them, provides for them and helps them?"

Then He, glorified be He, declared Himself free of this hideous assertion and said: ﴿Glory be to Allah above what they associate﴾, that is, above their associating (others) with Him, or above those they make partners to Him.

Then He, glorified be He, mentioned some of their ignorance and said: ﴿And if they should see a piece of the sky falling, they would say, "Layered clouds."﴾ Kisf is the plural of kisfah, which is a piece of a thing. The accusative of "sāqiṭan" (ساقِطًا) is circumstantial, or it is the second object. "Markum" means that which is piled up, one part upon another.

The meaning: If they were to see a piece of the sky falling upon them as punishment for them, they would not desist from their disbelief, but would say it is clouds piled up, one upon another. The differences of the readers regarding "kisfan" has already been mentioned.

Al-Akhfash said: Whoever reads "kisfan" (with a kasra on the kaf and a sukun on the sin) makes it singular, and whoever reads "kisafan" (with a kasra on the kaf and a fatḥa on the sin) makes it plural.

Then Allah, glorified be He, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to leave them, and said: ﴿So leave them until they meet their day in which they will be struck senseless﴾, that is, leave them and let them be until they meet the day of their death, or the day of their killing at Badr, or the Day of Resurrection.

The majority read "yulāqū" (يُلاقُوا); Abu Haywah read "yalqaw" (يَلْقَوْا). The majority read "yuṣ'aqūna" with the active form; Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim read it in the passive form. The ṣaʿqah (الصعقة) is destruction, as its explanation has already preceded.

﴿The day their plot will not avail them anything﴾: this is a substitute for "their day": that is, on that day their plot which they plotted against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in this world will not benefit them. ﴿Nor will they be helped﴾, that is, no helper will prevent the punishment descending upon them; rather, it will befall them without doubt.

﴿And indeed for those who have wronged there is a punishment besides that﴾, that is, for those who wronged themselves through disbelief and sins there is a punishment in this world, short of the punishment of the Day of Resurrection: that is, before it, and it is their being killed on the day of Badr.

Ibn Zayd said: It is the calamities of the world: pains, illnesses and afflictions, and the loss of wealth and children.

Mujahid said: It is hunger and hardship for seven years. It was said: it is the punishment of the grave. It was said: the intended punishment is drought, and the punishment that comes after it is their killing on the day of Badr. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾ what they will come to of Allah's punishment, and what He has prepared for them in this world and the Hereafter.

﴿And be patient for the judgment of your Lord﴾, until the punishment that We promised them befalls them. ﴿For indeed, you are in Our eyes﴾, that is, in Our sight and view, and in Our protection and safeguarding, so do not concern yourself with them.

Al-Zajjaj said: You are where We see you, guard you and watch over you, so they cannot reach you. ﴿And exalt your Lord with praise when you arise﴾, that is, declare your Lord free of what is unfitting for Him, joining that with praise of your Lord for His favor upon you, when you rise from your sitting place.

'Ata', Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Sufyan al-Thawri and Abu al-Ahwas said: He glorifies Allah when he rises from his sitting, saying: "Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi" or "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika" upon rising from every gathering he sits in.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b, al-Dahhak and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: When you rise to prayer.

Al-Dahhak said: He says: "Allahu akbar kabiran, wal-hamdu lillahi kathiran, wa subhan Allahi bukratan wa asilan." There is a difficulty in this, because the takbir occurs after rising, not during rising, and the tasbih occurs after the takbir, and this is not the meaning of the verse; so the first (view) is more preferable.

It was also said the meaning is: Pray to Allah when you rise from your sleep. Abu al-Jawza' and Hassan ibn 'Atiyyah said this.

Al-Kalbi said: Remember Allah with the tongue when you rise from your bed until you enter the prayer, which is the Fajr prayer.

﴿And during the night, glorify Him﴾: Allah, glorified be He, commanded him to glorify Him during part of the night. Muqatil said: that is, pray Maghrib and 'Isha'. It was also said: the two rak'ahs of Fajr. ﴿And after the setting of the stars﴾, that is, at the time of their receding at the end of the night. It was said: the Fajr prayer, and Ibn Jarir preferred this. It was also said: it is glorification during the receding of the prayers. The majority read "idbār" (إدبارَ) with a kasra on the hamza, as a verbal noun. Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, Muhammad ibn al-Sumayfa', Ya'qub and al-Minhal ibn 'Amr read it with a fatḥa on the hamza, as a plural: that is, the ends and backs of the stars when they set. "Dubur al-amr" means its last part. The discussion of this has already preceded in Surat Qaf.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Or are they the overseers?﴾ that he said: the dominant ones.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him: ﴿Or are they the ones who bring down?﴾

They also narrated from him regarding ﴿a punishment besides that﴾: that he said it is the punishment of the grave before the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Barzah al-Aslami who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in his later life, when he rose from a gathering, would say: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, ashhadu an la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayk.' A man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you say a statement you did not used to say before?' He said: 'It is an expiation for what occurs in the gathering.'"

Al-Nasa'i and al-Hakim also narrated it from the hadith of al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Rafi' ibn Khadij, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir narrated from Abu Hurayrah from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever sits in a gathering in which there is much noise, and says before he rises from his gathering: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, ashhadu an la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayk,' he will be forgiven for whatever occurred in that gathering."

al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan sahih.

Qatadah said: He says: Did you ask these people for a reward, so that it burdens them and they cannot accept Islam?

He, glorified be He, mocked their intellects, misled their minds and rebuked them: that is, they ascribe to Allah daughters, which are the weaker of the two kinds, and they assign to themselves sons, which are the higher of the two. This implies that whoever holds this view is in a lowly place in understanding and intellect, so it is not far-fetched from him to deny resurrection and reject monotheism.

Then He, glorified be He, returned to addressing His Messenger (ﷺ) and said: ﴿Or do you ask them for a payment?﴾ That is, "Rather, do you ask them for a payment they would give you for conveying the message?" ﴿So they are burdened with debt﴾, that is, burdened with an undertaking of a fine you demand from them: that is, they are overwhelmed by bearing that heavy debt.

Qatadah said: He says: Did you ask these people for a reward, so that it burdens them and they cannot accept Islam?

﴿Or do they have the unseen, so they write it down?﴾ That is, "Rather, do they claim that they have knowledge of the unseen, which is what is in the Preserved Tablet, so that they write for people whatever they wish of the knowledge of the unseen?"

Qatadah said: This is an answer to their saying: ﴿We await for him the misfortunes of time﴾. Allah says: Or do they have the unseen, so that they know Muhammad will die before them, so that they write it?

Ibn Qutaybah said: the meaning of "yaktubun" (يَكْتُبُونَ) is that they judge by what they say.

﴿Or do they intend a plot?﴾ That is, a scheme against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so that they destroy him by that scheme. ﴿Then those who disbelieve, they are the ones plotted against﴾, that is, the ones upon whom their scheme is turned and who will be repaid for their plotting; the harm of their plot returns to them. ﴿And the evil plot does not encompass except its people﴾ [Fatir: 43]. Allah killed them on the day of Badr and humiliated them on more than one occasion, and He, glorified be He, plotted against them: ﴿And they plotted, and Allah plotted, and Allah is the best of planners﴾ [Al 'Imran: 54].

﴿Or do they have a god other than Allah?﴾ That is, "Rather, do they claim that they have a god other than Allah who protects them, provides for them and helps them?"

Then He, glorified be He, declared Himself free of this hideous assertion and said: ﴿Glory be to Allah above what they associate﴾, that is, above their associating (others) with Him, or above those they make partners to Him.

Then He, glorified be He, mentioned some of their ignorance and said: ﴿And if they should see a piece of the sky falling, they would say, "Layered clouds."﴾ Kisf is the plural of kisfah, which is a piece of a thing. The accusative of "sāqiṭan" (ساقِطًا) is circumstantial, or it is the second object. "Markum" means that which is piled up, one part upon another.

The meaning: If they were to see a piece of the sky falling upon them as punishment for them, they would not desist from their disbelief, but would say it is clouds piled up, one upon another. The differences of the readers regarding "kisfan" has already been mentioned.

Al-Akhfash said: Whoever reads "kisfan" (with a kasra on the kaf and a sukun on the sin) makes it singular, and whoever reads "kisafan" (with a kasra on the kaf and a fatḥa on the sin) makes it plural.

Then Allah, glorified be He, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to leave them, and said: ﴿So leave them until they meet their day in which they will be struck senseless﴾, that is, leave them and let them be until they meet the day of their death, or the day of their killing at Badr, or the Day of Resurrection.

The majority read "yulāqū" (يُلاقُوا); Abu Haywah read "yalqaw" (يَلْقَوْا). The majority read "yuṣ'aqūna" with the active form; Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim read it in the passive form. The ṣaʿqah (الصعقة) is destruction, as its explanation has already preceded.

﴿The day their plot will not avail them anything﴾: this is a substitute for "their day": that is, on that day their plot which they plotted against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in this world will not benefit them. ﴿Nor will they be helped﴾, that is, no helper will prevent the punishment descending upon them; rather, it will befall them without doubt.

﴿And indeed for those who have wronged there is a punishment besides that﴾, that is, for those who wronged themselves through disbelief and sins there is a punishment in this world, short of the punishment of the Day of Resurrection: that is, before it, and it is their being killed on the day of Badr.

Ibn Zayd said: It is the calamities of the world: pains, illnesses and afflictions, and the loss of wealth and children.

Mujahid said: It is hunger and hardship for seven years. It was said: it is the punishment of the grave. It was said: the intended punishment is drought, and the punishment that comes after it is their killing on the day of Badr. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾ what they will come to of Allah's punishment, and what He has prepared for them in this world and the Hereafter.

﴿And be patient for the judgment of your Lord﴾, until the punishment that We promised them befalls them. ﴿For indeed, you are in Our eyes﴾, that is, in Our sight and view, and in Our protection and safeguarding, so do not concern yourself with them.

Al-Zajjaj said: You are where We see you, guard you and watch over you, so they cannot reach you. ﴿And exalt your Lord with praise when you arise﴾, that is, declare your Lord free of what is unfitting for Him, joining that with praise of your Lord for His favor upon you, when you rise from your sitting place.

'Ata', Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Sufyan al-Thawri and Abu al-Ahwas said: He glorifies Allah when he rises from his sitting, saying: "Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi" or "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika" upon rising from every gathering he sits in.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b, al-Dahhak and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: When you rise to prayer.

Al-Dahhak said: He says: "Allahu akbar kabiran, wal-hamdu lillahi kathiran, wa subhan Allahi bukratan wa asilan." There is a difficulty in this, because the takbir occurs after rising, not during rising, and the tasbih occurs after the takbir, and this is not the meaning of the verse; so the first (view) is more preferable.

It was also said the meaning is: Pray to Allah when you rise from your sleep. Abu al-Jawza' and Hassan ibn 'Atiyyah said this.

Al-Kalbi said: Remember Allah with the tongue when you rise from your bed until you enter the prayer, which is the Fajr prayer.

﴿And during the night, glorify Him﴾: Allah, glorified be He, commanded him to glorify Him during part of the night. Muqatil said: that is, pray Maghrib and 'Isha'. It was also said: the two rak'ahs of Fajr. ﴿And after the setting of the stars﴾, that is, at the time of their receding at the end of the night. It was said: the Fajr prayer, and Ibn Jarir preferred this. It was also said: it is glorification during the receding of the prayers. The majority read "idbār" (إدبارَ) with a kasra on the hamza, as a verbal noun. Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, Muhammad ibn al-Sumayfa', Ya'qub and al-Minhal ibn 'Amr read it with a fatḥa on the hamza, as a plural: that is, the ends and backs of the stars when they set. "Dubur al-amr" means its last part. The discussion of this has already preceded in Surat Qaf.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Or are they the overseers?﴾ that he said: the dominant ones.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him: ﴿Or are they the ones who bring down?﴾

They also narrated from him regarding ﴿a punishment besides that﴾: that he said it is the punishment of the grave before the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Barzah al-Aslami who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in his later life, when he rose from a gathering, would say: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, ashhadu an la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayk.' A man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you say a statement you did not used to say before?' He said: 'It is an expiation for what occurs in the gathering.'"

Al-Nasa'i and al-Hakim also narrated it from the hadith of al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Rafi' ibn Khadij, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir narrated from Abu Hurayrah from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever sits in a gathering in which there is much noise, and says before he rises from his gathering: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, ashhadu an la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayk,' he will be forgiven for whatever occurred in that gathering."

al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan sahih.

There are supported and mursal narrations on this topic.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And exalt your Lord with praise when you arise﴾ that he said: when you rise from your bed until you enter into prayer.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Hurayrah from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding His saying: ﴿And during the night, glorify Him﴾ that he said: "The two rak'ahs before the Fajr prayer."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿and after the setting of the stars﴾ that he said: the two rak'ahs of Fajr.
